Good idea. Comparatives are very useful at work. Before we start: when you compare two things, which two words or endings do you already use?

Our goal today: compare two things clearly, with the correct comparative form and the word "than".

Here is a model sentence in a work setting: "The morning meeting is shorter than the afternoon meeting."

Now your task. Think of two things at your job, for example two tasks, two tools or two schedules. Write one sentence that compares them. Try it in your own words, and we will look at the language together afterwards.

Yes! You know "I work". Now look at he, she and it.

Anna walks to school every day.

After he, she or it, we add -s to the verb.

Right: "He sings every day." Wrong: "He sing every day."

Your turn. Write the correct form of the verb:
The cat ___ (sleep) on my bed.
(Answer with only the verb.)

Yes! We compare things when we say one is more or less than another.

A horse is taller than a dog.

For a short word, add -er and then use "than".

Right: "A rabbit is faster than a turtle." Wrong: "A rabbit is more fast than a turtle."

Your turn. Write the correct form:
A mouse is ___ (small) than a cat.
